summary: Async pin commit fragmentation causes rolling rollback loop and mixed canary routing
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (SparkFit Inc.) observed bursty tenant requests that were expected to remain pinned to a newly-promoted model variant during a staged canary rollout. Instead, some sessions oscillated between the canary and legacy variants and several tenants experienced transparent fallback to degraded variant during a scheduled promote/commit window.

Impact:
- Intermittent mixed-model responses for 12 tenants over a 45-minute window (some prompts returned embeddings from legacy model while text-generation used canary).
- Increased tail latency (95th percentile +120ms) and two customer-facing errors where the stream truncated.
- Billing spike observed from duplicated request replays (approx +18% token usage in the window).

Environment:
- Prod (us-west primary, eu-central mirrored).
- Staged canary rollout for redwood-v2-13b-quant (weight ramp 5% -> 20%).
- Tenant routing policy: tenant-level pin with explicit model selection on request header X-Model-Pin.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Promote canary redwood-v2-13b-quant to 10% cohort with tenant pin enabled.
2) Initiate parallel streaming sessions for affected tenants using chunked upload + keepalive.
3) During the commit window, trigger a prewarm (control-plane initiated) and then a scheduled autoscaler preempt (spot eviction in us-west).
4) Observe variant switching mid-stream for a subset of sessions; some sessions show duplicated upstream calls.

Expected behavior:
- Tenant sessions explicitly pinned to the canary should remain bound for the duration of the pin/grace window or fail closed to legacy rather than interleaving outputs.

Observed behavior:
- Pin commit appears to fragment across orchestrator shards; some shards applied the commit while others reverted to previous snapshot triggering a rollback loop.
- Edge retriers replayed inflight requests to fallback paths which produced mixed outputs and doubled token counts for affected requests.

Logs/Telemetry attached (customer supplied):
- Trace IDs (sample): trace-usw-9981a, trace-euc-2201c
- Edge logs show 502->fallback path for tenant T-7312 at 2026-03-10T14:21:05Z.
- Orchestrator commit logs show shard commit time skew ~1.2s and two conflicting snapshot merges.

Additional notes:
- Customer is on enterprise SLA; this impacted production user-facing endpoints and required escalation.

investigation_notes: Hypothesis A: Orchestrator shard snapshot merge race - during concurrent prewarm and autoscaler spot eviction the commit message propagates before all shards have applied the new model snapshot. Edges trust the coordinator and route based on partial state causing pin fragmentation.

Hypothesis B: Edge retrier behavior - inflight streaming requests that hit a 502 on a shard were retried to a fallback pool which evaluated routing metadata differently and used legacy variant, leading to mixed outputs and doubled token usage.

Reproduction steps ran in staging: mirrored traffic with artificially induced autoscaler preempt -> reproduced fragmentation 3/10 attempts. Adding 200ms serialization at commit reduced rate to 0/30 reproductions.

Key logs: orchestrator/apply_shard.shard_id=17 commit_seq=2034 apply_duration_ms=12, shard_id=22 apply_duration_ms=1220, coordinator emitted commit_published before all shard applies completed.
See gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood-support/async-pin-2712023

Related PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1298 (adds prewarm concurrency), https://github.com/redwood-inference/orchestrator/pull/3412 (candidate fix to shard commit ack).
Customer repro artifacts: compressed traces uploaded to S3: s3://redwood-support/artifacts/SUP-2712023/traces.zip (internal access only).

Mitigation tested: quarantine commit-exposure behind per-epoch shard ack (feature-flag). Rolling flag to canary reduced mixed-routing incidents to zero in mirror for 12h. Performance cost: median commit time increased by ~30ms in test.
resolution:
Mitigation applied: feature-flag 'require-shard-acks-before-commit-exposed' enabled for affected region (us-west) and customer cohort. Orchestrator eng merged patch to serialize commit publication (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/orchestrator/pull/3412) and scheduled staged rollout to remaining regions after additional smoke tests.

Workaround for customer: We recommended clients to backoff and avoid parallel keepalive reconnects in the 10s commit window. Support initiated billing adjustment review for duplicated requests; finance to follow up.

Follow-up actions:
- Roll out orchestrator fix to eu-central after 24h of smoke testing.
- Add end-to-end test to CI that simulates prewarm+autoscaler eviction during commit (ticket INT-4402).
- Documented runbook update: ensure commit visibility only after quorum of shard apply acks (Confluence page updated).

Status: fix merged; mitigation deployed to customer region behind flag; monitoring shows no recurrence in 24h mirror window. Billing follow-up pending.
next_steps: Roll out orchestrator PR to eu-central and validate in mirror traffic (target 2026-03-13).
